title: Grade 5 Science — Tue, Jun 10
description: The Digestive System — Day 2 of 5: Stomach and small intestine
subject: science

questions.question: After the oesophagus, food enters the:
questions.explanation: From the oesophagus, food enters the stomach, where further digestion takes place.

questions.question: The stomach produces ____ to break down food.
questions.explanation: The stomach produces gastric juice containing hydrochloric acid and enzymes that digest proteins and kill bacteria.

questions.question: The acid in the stomach is:
questions.explanation: The stomach produces hydrochloric acid (HCl) which creates the acidic environment needed to digest proteins and kill germs.

questions.question: The semi-liquid food that leaves the stomach is called:
questions.explanation: After mixing with gastric juices in the stomach, food becomes a semi-liquid paste called chyme.

questions.question: The small intestine is where most ____ takes place.
options: Absorption of nutrients into the blood
questions.explanation: The small intestine is the main site of digestion completion and nutrient absorption into the bloodstream.

questions.question: The inner walls of the small intestine have tiny finger-like projections called:
questions.explanation: Villi (singular: villus) greatly increase the surface area of the small intestine for efficient nutrient absorption.

questions.question: Which organ produces bile which helps digest fats?
questions.explanation: The liver produces bile, a green-yellow liquid that breaks down fats into tiny droplets for easier digestion.

questions.question: Bile is stored in the:
questions.explanation: Bile is produced by the liver and stored in the gall bladder until it is needed in the small intestine.

questions.question: The pancreas produces digestive juices that are released into the:
questions.explanation: The pancreas releases pancreatic juice containing enzymes into the small intestine to digest carbohydrates, proteins, and fats.

questions.question: Which enzyme breaks down proteins in the stomach?
questions.explanation: Pepsin is the main enzyme in the stomach that breaks down proteins into smaller peptide chains.

questions.question: The small intestine is approximately ____ long in an adult.
questions.explanation: Despite being called 'small', the small intestine is about 6–7 metres long in adults — longer than the large intestine.

questions.question: Why is the small intestine called 'small' if it is actually longer?
options: It is smaller in diameter (width) than the large intestine
It only handles small food particles
questions.explanation: It is called 'small' because its diameter (about 2.5 cm) is much narrower than the large intestine (about 6 cm).

questions.question: Absorbed nutrients from the small intestine enter the:
questions.explanation: Villi contain tiny blood capillaries. Absorbed nutrients pass through villi walls into the blood and are carried to body cells.

questions.question: Which enzyme in the small intestine breaks down fats?
questions.explanation: Lipase (from the pancreas) breaks down fats into fatty acids and glycerol, which can then be absorbed.

questions.question: What is the role of bile in fat digestion?
options: It directly digests fats using enzymes
It emulsifies fats — breaks large fat droplets into smaller ones for lipase to act on
It absorbs fats into the blood
It creates acid for fat digestion
questions.explanation: Bile emulsifies fats — breaking large fat globules into tiny droplets. This increases the surface area for lipase to work on.
